analyst_view.overall: Manchester United are 19th with 8 points and in deep trouble. Mauricio Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick in mid-November, lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first game, and this is his first home match. Leny Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on appeal on 24 November, so he is available, although the numbers assumed he would be out. Benjamin Sesko (shin, out until at least January) and Baleba are also out, and United play Sporting in Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, so they have only three days to recover. Brentford are 6th after beating 10-man Everton 4-0 on Monday, but their first-choice striker Igor Thiago is serving the last two games of a three-match ban from his red card at Brighton. He misses this game, and the numbers do not know that. Brentford are also without Aaron Hickey, Nathan Collins, Rico Henry and others. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.6 each, and already count United leaking 19 goals in their last six games and Brentford scoring well. Brentford will be without Igor Thiago, their main striker, who misses this game through suspension; the numbers don't know that, and the 34-year-old Callum Wilson is the likely stand-in. Yoro's ban was overturned, but as a defender his return barely changes the numbers, so I go about 6% lower, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners: 6.0 for United and 4.4 for Brentford, with recent form and past meetings already counted. Pochettino wants a high-pressing, front-foot United at home, which fits the home side winning most of the corners. Thiago's absence matters less for corners than for goals, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.9 cards and already count United's rising card count and past meetings. A struggling side under a new manager could make for a scrappy game, but there is no derby edge, no referee has been named, and Brentford's ban is already being served, so I don't have a clear reason to move. I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.8 shots, 19.2 of them from United, with recent form counted. Brentford lose Thiago's shooting and presence, and United come off a Champions League trip to Lisbon three days earlier, which could cost them some energy. I take about 4% off, to about 28.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 9.9 shots on target, including 4.1 for Brentford, helped by how many United have allowed lately. Without Thiago, the striker who gets most of Brentford's chances on target, their finishing should be weaker, and the numbers can't see the ban. I go about 5% lower, to about 9.4.
